en.title: ea
en.summary: This is the letter L317 from the vowel-consonant groups.

sections.title: Sounds of ea
paragraphs: The letters ea have no single name. They usually make a vowel sound, as in (eat) /iːt/, which means to take food. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. The letters ea make three different sounds across English words.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift your tongue high and push it forward. Spread your lips wide and make a voiced sound. For the second sound, lower your tongue slightly and keep your mouth half open. For the third sound, glide your tongue smoothly from a mid vowel up toward a close vowel. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake.

sections.title: Reading the spelling
paragraphs: The letters ea most commonly make the vowel in (meat) /miːt/. Before letters like d, th, or l, they often make the short vowel in (bread) /brɛd/. In a few special words, the letters make the diphthong in (great) /ɡreɪt/. A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable, where the sound glides from the first to the second.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: Do not say (head) /hɛd/ with the vowel of (eat) /iːt/. Keep the vowel short and open your mouth slightly more. Do not say (steak) /steɪk/ with the long vowel sound either. Glide your tongue from the first sound to the second instead.
